# Rice's whale eDNA wgs

Goal: can we use non-biopsy samples to obtain whole genome data from Rice's whales? 
Samples being tested:
- Tube juice
- fluke prints
- Bones

The hope is that we can obtain 

1. Mitochondrial genomes for every samples
2. Low coverage WGS. At a minimum identify duplicate individuals. Ideally with good enough data to use for population genetics.

## Nuclear genome

### Number of reads and mapping success

```{r}
#| label: load-data

library(tidyverse)

qc <- read_tsv("../qc_report.tsv") |>
  rename(genome_cov = `% genome_cov`) |>
  mutate(
    pct_genome_cov = genome_cov * 100,
    sample_type = case_when(
      sample %in% c("Bric026", "Bric032") ~ "Biopsy",
      sample %in% c("Bric045", "Bric046") ~ "Bone",
      str_detect(sample, "^Bric_tag") ~ "Tube juice",
      str_detect(sample, "^Bric_eDNA") ~ "Fluke print"
    ),
    sample_type = factor(
      sample_type,
      levels = c("Biopsy", "Bone", "Tube juice", "Fluke print")
    )
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-qc
#| tbl-cap: "Sequencing and mapping summary for each sample."

qc |>
  arrange(sample_type, desc(percent_mapped)) |>
  mutate(reads_m = reads_after_filtering / 1e6) |>
  select(
    Sample = sample,
    Type = sample_type,
    `Reads after filtering (M)` = reads_m,
    `% mapped` = percent_mapped,
    `% duplicates` = percent_duplicates,
    `Mean depth (×)` = mean_depth,
    `% genome covered` = pct_genome_cov
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 2, 1))
```

Note that mean depth is from the entire genome, counting 0's. 

## Nuclear genome

General idea:  
`Align to reference genome -> pseudohaploidize known SNP sites -> id relatedness/duplicate individuals.` 

The pseudohaploid approach and pairwise mismatch rate (pmr) is what is used in ancient DNA with poor data and other low coverage data so quite similar to our data: 
- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/mec.70375
- https://github.com/hringbauer/cayo_pmr


Calculate PMR:

`pseudoHap_filter_merge_replicates.ipynb`


### relatedness

`pmr_breadr.R`

I also did it manually in `pseudoHap_filter_merge_replicates.ipynb`, but seems safe to do it with breadr for now. 

![](../figures/pmr_nonmaskedGenome_nonmasked-PH.png)

This is strange. Many of the eDNA samples are identical. Check the actual values when comparing to high coverage samples:


```{r}
#| label: tbl-pmr
pmr <- read_csv("../pmr_out.csv")

pmr |>
  slice_head(n = 15) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

Many/most seem to be most related to Bric006- this is the reference individual. This suggests there is reference bias. Check this below. 


### Reference Bias

`ref_bias.R`

Overall conclusion: Flukeprint samples did not work. Tube juice and bone samples look OK. 

![](../figures/reference_bias_nonmaskedGenome_nonmasked-PH.png)

Clearly biased towards the reference allele. 100%!

Solution: Mask the reference genome at known SNPs, from the RW preprint. Then re-align to this. In theory, this should help. 

![](../figures/reference_bias_maskedGenome_masked-PH.png)

Now they're 50%. This suggests the SNPs are being randomly called and are not real.
